## Remedial Assignment — CAT-2 {.smaller}

**Coverage:** Module 3 partial, Module 4 full, Module 5 up to DMA

**Submit:** written solutions with all steps, diagrams wherever needed.

| Module | CAT-2 weight | Questions |
|---|---:|---:|
| M3 — Instruction cycle, control, performance | 10 marks | 2 |
| M4 — Memory systems and cache | 25 marks | 5 |
| M5 — I/O and DMA | 15 marks | 3 |
| **Total** | **50 marks** | **10** |

::: {.notes}
Questions are adapted from BCSE205L CAT-2 PYQP patterns.
:::

## Module 3 — Instruction Cycle, Control, Performance {.smaller}

1. Three processors execute the same ISA.

   | Processor | Clock rate | CPI |
   |---|---:|---:|
   | P1 | 3 GHz | 1.5 |
   | P2 | 2.5 GHz | 1.0 |
   | P3 | 4 GHz | 2.2 |

   Determine the highest-performance processor. If each runs a program for 10 s, calculate cycles and instruction count. If execution time must reduce by 30% while CPI rises by 20%, find the new required clock rate.

2. Compare **hardwired** and **microprogrammed** control units. For adding 30 new CPU instructions, which control approach is easier to extend? Justify with design complexity, speed, and flexibility.

## Module 4 — Memory Systems and Cache I {.smaller}

3. A computer uses `1024 x 8` RAM chips and `1024 x 8` ROM chips. It requires `2K x 8` RAM, `2K x 8` ROM, and four interface units with four registers each. Higher-order address bits assign `00` to RAM, `01` to ROM, and `10` to interface registers. Find chip count, address map, hexadecimal ranges, and chip layout.

4. A byte-addressable memory has 64 bytes and 4-way **high-order interleaving**. For CPU address `101100`, identify module-select bits, location-select bits, selected module, byte location, and sketch the memory organization.

5. A system needs `512K x 32` byte-addressable RAM using `64K x 8` RAM chips. Design an interleaved memory system: total chips, number of banks, chips per bank, bank-select address lines, and decoder logic. Then repeat if expanded to `1M x 32`.

## Module 4 — Memory Systems and Cache II {.smaller}

6. A 2-way set-associative cache has 8 total cache lines. Main memory has 128 blocks. Starting with empty cache, use **optimal replacement** for this reference string:

   `5, 2, 3, 7, 3, 15, 14, 2, 1, 21, 13, 72, 12, 5, 19, 3, 2, 1, 22, 9, 26, 10, 5, 1, 7, 26, 14, 9, 19, 26`

   Show final cache contents, hit ratio, and miss ratio.

7. A fully associative cache has 4 blocks, block size 1 word, initially empty. For references

   `10, 20, 30, 40, 10, 20, 10, 50, 20, 30, 10, 20, 30, 40, 10`

   simulate FIFO and LRU. Compute hit ratio, miss ratio, compulsory misses, and conflict/capacity misses. State which policy performs better.

## Module 5 — I/O and DMA {.smaller}

8. A disk transfers data to memory using DMA at `10 MB/s`. Processor speed is `600 MHz`. It takes 300 cycles to initiate and 900 cycles to complete a DMA transfer. For a `20 KB` block, calculate percentage of processor time consumed.

9. Explain the role of an I/O interface module in the I/O subsystem. Draw a neat block diagram and include address decoding, control interpretation, data synchronization, and peripheral controller interaction.

10. For a DMA controller in a microcontroller system, list and explain the three key registers programmed by the CPU before transfer. Recommend a DMA transfer mode for time-critical high-bandwidth communication and justify.
